messages.subject: =~ versus ~~
parts:
I'm sure this is an extremely basic question - so I apologize. I'm new to SEM.  I've read and read about latent variables (=~) and covarying (~~), but I still don't understand the difference.  I thought latent variables measured the variance and covariance between and among items.  So, I thought that this:

KP =~ Q2 + Q5 + Q7 + Q9

would be the same thing as this:

Q2~~ Q5 + Q7 + Q9
Q5 ~~ Q7 + Q9
Q7 ~~ Q9

But when I ran a model using the second code, I got significantly higher fit indices than when I ran the model using the first code.

Why is that? Clearly I don't understand the difference between latent variables and covarying.  If someone can point me to some resources that can explain the difference in my example models above, I'd really appreciate it.

Thank you!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: =~ versus ~~
parts:
The second syntax imposes no constraints on the covariance matrix of the four observed variables. There are as many free parameters (6 covariances plus variances) as there are unique elements of the covariance matrix. the first syntax specifies that all covariances among the observed variables are accounted for by their joint dependence on a single common factor. This syntax specifies only 8 free parameters (4 loadings plus 4 residual variances). The nature of the constraints involves proportional ratios of covariances. For any two congeneric observed variables (loading on the same single common factor and without residual covariances), it must be true that:

covariance (1, 3) / covariance (2, 3) = constant across all other third variables.
